thread:
maria (PM): heads up - we need a short ops/playbook for onboarding customers into committed reserved pools that want bursty workloads across regions. the ask: minimize cold-start latency while keeping autoscale predictable and cost-contained.

dan (Eng): can you scope the exact problems we're solving? eg is this prewarm, KV cache warmup, routing, or quota shaping?

maria (PM): all of the above. customers are seeing long tails at the first megabyte of traffic after a quiet period, and they want a contract with burst guarantees. they expect us to avoid a full dedicated warmup cost all the time.

lee (SRE): oncall sees two failure modes: (1) sudden tenant ramp overwhelms a regional micro-pool and causes 503s, (2) our prewarm + autoscale overshoots and wastes GPUs. want explicit thresholds for admit vs. prewarm.

ana (CS): specific ask from Lighthouse customer: guarantee 95p latency < 250ms for first 2k tokens during a burst window up to 5m, with a low-cost standby mode between bursts. they will pay for predictable headroom but not full-time prewarm.

dan (Eng): proposal: introduce "burst-warmup slots" concept. tenants buy N standby slots per-region. slots are lightweight (no pinned GPUs) but trigger instant prefix cache provisioning + fast-path routing into a hot lane when used. autoscale then adds GPUs if sustained beyond warmup TTL.

maria (PM): sounds good. what are the config knobs?

dan (Eng): knobs: 
- standby_slots: integer per-region
- warmup_ttl: seconds (default 300)
- fastpath_max_concurrency: qps before we escalate to full GPU allocation
- prewarm_credit: budgeted ephemeral GPU time if warm traffic persists

lee (SRE): need hard limits to avoid noisy neighbors: max_standby_per_pool, per-tenant burst_rate_limit, and a soft-fail path to fallback model variant (smaller context, cheaper) if capacity unavailable.

sam (Data): telemetry signals we need for rollout: 
- 95/99 latency during first-token vs steady-state
- queue length and rejection rate per-tenant during warmup
- GPU spin-up count and duration triggered by each tenant
- cost delta (GPU-mins) vs baseline

maria (PM): launch criteria suggestion: 
1) canary w/ 3 customers in us-west/us-east for 2 weeks under synthetic and live traffic
2) <1% increased 95p infra errors attributable to warmups
3) cost uplift < 12% for participating customers (we can bill or offset)

ana (CS): CS wants a customer-facing statement: "standby slots provide fast warmup to burst windows; sustained traffic will incur reserved allocation charges after warmup TTL". we'll add an onboarding checklist for expectations.

dan (Eng): implementation notes: routing component needs a new tag on requests: `fastpath=true|false`. simple example: 
```
policy {
  if tenant.standby_slots > 0 and recent_idle < warmup_ttl then route fastpath
  else normal pool routing
}
```
Also we should ensure LB health checks don't wrongly evict standby allocations.

lee (SRE): ops runbook items: 
- alert: sustained fallback to model-variant >30s
- alert: >5 spin-ups in 1m from same tenant
- rollback knob: global feature flag to disable fastpath per-region

maria (PM): prioritization: we should ship minimal fastpath + telemetry first, then billing & product UI second. timeline idea: 2 sprints for infra + canary, +1 sprint for billing and docs.

sam (Data): can start instrumenting now if Eng exposes `fastpath` tag in logs. I'll draft the dashboards.

ana (CS): add legal ask: must include explicit SLA language for burst windows in contracts. I'll draft with Sales.

dan (Eng): open questions: how do we account for multi-region bursts where tenant uses standby in two regions concurrently? double-charge or coordinated allowance?

maria (PM): product decision: allow cross-region standby but cap total concurrent standby_slots across regions to tenant.standby_limit_global. prefer coordinated allowance for conservative billing.

lee (SRE): one more: make warmup_ttl configurable per-tenant so latency-sensitive customers can set shorter TTLs if they pay. but default must be restrictive to control cost.

maria (PM): agreed. next steps: 
- Dan: draft PR for `fastpath` tag + routing rule (due EOW)
- Sam: dashboard skeleton for warmup metrics (due EOW)
- Lee: ops alert runbook and feature-flag toggle (due next Tue)
- Ana: customer onboarding blurb draft (due next Tue)
- Maria: ownership of canary plan and launch criteria doc (I'll assemble)

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-service v2.41 -> staging in 3m :rocket:

ana (CS): quick note: +1 from Lighthouse on principle. they asked for a pilot next month. I'll coordinate dates after we have canary doc. :thumbsup:

maria (PM): thanks team — keeping thread for final canary checklist and signoffs.
